scope: Availability/lineage audit of specific pinned sources and release endpoints. No completeness guarantee over every historical branch or external weight host; no new strength claim.

entries.kind: Qt6 GUI and UCI client, not a new independent engine
entries.license: MIT application; referenced external engine and weights have separate terms
entries.finding: README explicitly delegates Xiangqi/Jieqi play to official Pikafish branches. Recursive tree has no network/model; releases endpoint returned an empty list. Its weight-compatibility/download investigations are author-reported leads, not independently reproduced here.
entries.coverage: Deduplicate GUI against its actual engine; do not count it as another defeated AI.

entries.finding: Release endpoint returned no releases; full recursive trees of jieqi/ablation contain no .nnue model or packaged engine archive. The pinned jieqi evaluate.h also requires pikafish.nnue; README links generic Xiangqi network sites, which does not establish a compatible trained Jieqi weight. Exact model remains unresolved.
entries.license: GPL source; separate restrictive personal/noncommercial NNUE terms in the pinned master. No weights redistributed or license-equivalence claim.
entries.coverage: Unverified neural baseline; do not substitute an arbitrary Xiangqi/ABJ weight or random network.

entries.finding: Pinned Python self-play and loader reference a safetensors network. JSON files are architecture configurations, not numerical weights. Full pinned tree contains no .safetensors/.pt/.pth/.nnue/.onnx archive; release endpoint returned none. C++ PIMCTS and actor/judge viewpoint bookkeeping exist; neural runtime strength cannot be measured without the original model.
entries.license: Inherited C++ chess files carry LCZero GPL-3.0-or-later headers with CUDA additional permission. game/LICENSE contains pybind BSD terms. Root project license absent and newly authored Python/search licensing remains unresolved; neither all-unlicensed nor all-BSD is established.
entries.coverage: Distinct neural search candidate stays visible and unverified; an untrained replacement would not represent its strength.

research_context.title: On the complexity of Dark Chinese Chess
research_context.finding: The primary paper studies full-board Jieqi and private hidden captures, uses random-move self-play for complexity estimation with40 no-capture plies, and notes that off-board hidden status need not be considered when that color has no dark piece on board. This is prior context for abstraction, not a supplied trained strong baseline or evidence of a new fundamental observation by this project.
